comments.body:
## Implemented — committed, awaiting `make verify` then Gerrit

Commit `bf6e64c0993` on branch `fix-011f-autodeploy`
(Change-Id `Ic515e0d27f7e66decb02569e67710e4d9598064d`).

### Changes

`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`:
- New `mcp_running_port_of()` reads the port from `docker port` — **runtime** state, which
  only resolves for a running container — as opposed to `mcp_port_of()`, which reads
  `HostConfig.PortBindings`, i.e. **historical intent** that an exited container still
  carries. That distinction is the whole defect.
- New `mcp_running_backend_on_port()` returns the running managed container bound to a
  given host port.
- `mcp_live_backend_name()` now consults that first and only falls through to the
  `HostConfig` scan when no running container owns the live port. The fallback's real
  purpose — finding a live backend that has genuinely died — is untouched.
- `mcp_retire_sweep()` now retains by container **identity** (`$n = $live_name`) rather
  than by port equality (`$p = $live`). That is what un-strands the exited container:
  previously any container whose historical port merely collided with the live port was
  retained as "nginx still points here" and so was never reaped.

### Acceptance criteria

- [x] Live-backend resolution prefers a running managed container owning the live nginx
      port; the `PortBindings` fallback applies only when no running one owns it.
- [x] The retire sweep reaps an exited stale container whose historical port collides with
      the live port and which is not the live running backend.
- [x] Regression test covers the three-deploy ping-pong (8092 → 8093 → 8092) and asserts no
      `mcp-live-backend-down` marker while a healthy running backend owns the live port.
- [x] Regression test asserts the marker is STILL emitted when the live backend has
      genuinely died.
- [ ] `rebar-autodeploy-errors` returns to OK — verifiable only after the fix reaches the
      box.
- [ ] The stranded `rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092` is reaped by the fixed sweep — same.

### Evidence

The ping-pong test was confirmed RED before the fix, and for the right reason: it did not
merely fail an assertion, it showed the detector selecting the exited container and
*self-healing it* —

    cmds=['start rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092']
    mcp self-heal: restarted live backend rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092 on 127.0.0.1:8092
    AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "mcp-live-backend-down", ...}

which reproduces the production signature exactly. Both tests pass after the fix, and the
full `tests/scripts/test_autodeploy_mcp_bluegreen.py` harness is green at 63 passed.
`make check` is clean, including `check_shellcheck.py` and `check_deploy_manifest.py`
(12 derived deploy-relevant paths all covered).

Assertions are structural — on emitted markers and on which container was acted upon —
with no wall-clock budgets, so there is nothing here to flake under runner contention.

The last two criteria are deliberately left open: they are on-box observations that can
only be made after this lands and a timer tick runs. A one-time manual `docker rm` would
clear the alarm now, but it would not fix the defect and the state recurs on the next port
ping-pong, so it was not applied.

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`rebar-autodeploy-errors` has been in ALARM continuously since 2026-09-20T11:01Z,
emitting an `AUTODEPLOY_ERROR` marker on every `rebar-autodeploy.timer` tick. The
alarm condition is FALSE: MCP is healthy, production is at `main` tip, and the
review gate is fully functional. The marker is produced by a defect in the MCP
live-backend self-heal detector, which selects an EXITED container from an older
deploy as the "live" backend.

This is not cosmetic. A permanently-firing `mcp-live-backend-down` marker means a
REAL MCP backend outage is now invisible -- the alarm can no longer distinguish
the two, so the signal it exists to carry has been destroyed.

## Verbatim evidence

Still firing at the time of writing:

    2026-09-20T13:19:34+0000 autodeploy.sh[865945]: AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"ts": 1789910374,
      "reason": "mcp-live-backend-down",
      "detail": "live mcp backend rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092 on port 8092 is NOT running;
       /mcp is failing. Retained (never reaped: nginx still points here);
       awaiting restart/redeploy"}
    2026-09-20T13:19:34+0000 autodeploy.sh[865945]: {"event":"autodeploy","ts":1789910374,
      "msg":"up to date (e84e4c5e9439bcfd27875d152de36eb40eb4f46b); no-op"}

Note the pairing: the SAME tick reports `up to date ... no-op` while also claiming
the live backend is down. Those two cannot both be true, which is the tell.

Onset, showing the detector firing one second before the redeploy it demands:

    11:01:20Z msg: "mcp cutover complete: /mcp upstream now 127.0.0.1:8092 (deploy DONE...)"
    11:01:20Z msg: "mcp retire: 'docker stop --time 1260' rebar-mcp-feca8a211eea-8093 ..."
    11:01:20Z AUTODEPLOY_ERROR {"reason": "mcp-live-backend-down",
                "detail": "live mcp backend rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092 ... is NOT running"}
    11:01:21Z msg: "mcp redeployed + healthy at 127.0.0.1:8092"

## Root cause

Latent bug introduced by Gerrit change **2825**, commit
`7f014af789038785b9d79dc713bf1d72b20e5747` ("Restart dead MCP live backend"), which
added `mcp_live_backend_name()` / `mcp_self_heal_live_backend()` to
`infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh` together with a `HostConfig.PortBindings` fallback so
that an EXITED container can still be mapped to a port.

Triggered by an ordinary port ping-pong across three consecutive deploys:

1. change 3004 (`c0b1ad2e8e9`) ran MCP on port **8092**.
2. change 3006 (`feca8a211ee`) cut MCP over to **8093** and stopped the 8092 container,
   leaving `rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092` in state `exited`.
3. change 3007 (`e84e4c5e943`) cut MCP back to **8092**, creating the real live
   container `rebar-mcp-e84e4c5e9439-8092`.

Now TWO containers resolve to port 8092 -- the exited `c0b1ad2e8e92` one via the
`HostConfig.PortBindings` fallback, and the genuine running `e84e4c5e9439` one. The
detector selects the exited container, reports it as the live backend, finds it not
running, and emits the marker. Because it also RETAINS it ("never reaped: nginx still
points here"), the stale container is never cleaned up and the loop is self-perpetuating.

The `PortBindings` fallback is correct in isolation -- its purpose is to identify a
live backend that has died. The defect is that it is consulted even when a RUNNING
managed container already owns the live port, so a historical port binding outranks
present reality.

## Marker rate

67 markers from 11:01Z to 13:19Z, bucketed per 15 minutes: 7, 8, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 3.
That is ~one marker per `rebar-autodeploy.timer` tick (~2 min), NOT one per deploy
backoff. This explains the observed CloudWatch rate of 5-9 per 15-minute period, which
was otherwise inconsistent with the alarm's `BACKOFF_CAP=900s` design assumption.

## What is NOT wrong (measured, so the fix stays scoped)

- Production is NOT behind. `/var/lib/rebar/deployed-sha`, `bot-deployed-sha` and
  `mcp-deployed-sha` all read `e84e4c5e9439bcfd27875d152de36eb40eb4f46b`, equal to
  `origin/main`; behind-count 0.
- MCP is genuinely healthy: nginx points at `server 127.0.0.1:8092`, local `8092/health`
  reports store present and handshake OK, public unauth `/mcp` returns 401 as designed,
  and the `mcp_healthy` metric is 1.0.
- The Gerrit review gate is unaffected. `/review/health` returns
  `{"status":"ok","in_flight":0,"queue_depth":0,"gerrit_auth":"ok"}`,
  `compose-review-bot-1` is `Up (healthy)`, and change 3008 received `LLM-Review+1`
  at 12:25:14Z. The autodeploy fail-safe claim holds.

So this is exclusively a detector-selection defect. Do not widen it into a deploy or
MCP-health change.

## Fix

In `infra/scripts/autodeploy.sh`:

1. Live-backend resolution must prefer a RUNNING managed container that owns the current
   nginx live port. Consult the `HostConfig.PortBindings` fallback ONLY when no running
   managed container owns that port -- which preserves the fallback's original purpose
   (detecting a live backend that has genuinely died) while preventing a historical
   binding from outranking a running container.
2. The retire sweep must be able to reap an exited stale container whose historical
   `HostConfig` port collides with the current live port but whose identity is not the
   current live running backend. Without this, an already-stranded container stays
   stranded after the detector is fixed.

Portability note: this is a host-side shell script driven by a systemd timer, not a
CI-provider capability, so no CI-specific trigger is involved and the
`project.portability` criterion is not engaged.

A one-time on-box `docker rm` of the exited `rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092` would clear
the current alarm immediately, but it is an operator action, it does not fix the defect,
and the same state will recur on the next port ping-pong. It was deliberately NOT applied.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Live-backend resolution prefers a running managed container owning the live nginx port; the `PortBindings` fallback applies only when no running managed container owns it.
- [ ] The retire sweep reaps an exited stale container whose historical port collides with the live port and which is not the live running backend.
- [ ] A regression test covers the three-deploy port ping-pong (port A -> port B -> port A) and asserts no `mcp-live-backend-down` marker is emitted while a healthy running backend owns the live port.
- [ ] A regression test asserts the detector STILL emits the marker when the live backend has genuinely died, so the fallback's real purpose is preserved.
- [ ] `rebar-autodeploy-errors` returns to OK, verified against the `rebar/host:deploy_errors` metric after the fix reaches the box.
- [ ] The stranded `rebar-mcp-c0b1ad2e8e92-8092` container is reaped, by the fixed sweep rather than by hand.
